abstract.para: Load the default boot entry with kexec-bootloader, then reboot with systemctl kexec.

topic.para: The kexec-tools package provides the kexec command. kexec-bootloader, which loads the default boot entry, is part of the update-bootloader package. Both packages are installed by default. To confirm that they are present:

important.title: A &kexec; reboot skips the firmware and the boot menu
important.para: A &kexec; reboot does not run the firmware and does not show the GRUB boot menu, so you cannot select another boot entry. kexec-bootloader loads the default boot entry with the kernel options that are currently set in the boot loader configuration. Changes in /etc/default/grub that you have not applied yet are included.

step.para: Make sure no important services are running and no users other than yourself are logged in, since a &kexec; reboot restarts the system immediately once triggered.
Optional: Check which kernel, initrd and kernel options will be loaded, without loading anything:
step.screen: Image : /usr/lib/modules/6.12.0-160099.49-default/vmlinuz Initrd : /boot/initrd-6.12.0-160099.49-default Append : splash=silent mitigations=auto quiet security=selinux crashkernel=72M,low crashkernel=394M,high Root : root=UUID=b06935f0-ff2e-49e7-9aec-e72b252abc7d Kexec call: kexec --kexec-syscall-auto --load '/usr/lib/modules/6.12.0-160099.49-default/vmlinuz' --initrd='/boot/initrd-6.12.0-160099.49-default' --append='root=UUID=b06935f0-ff2e-49e7-9aec-e72b252abc7d splash=silent mitigations=auto quiet security=selinux crashkernel=72M,low crashkernel=394M,high'

step.para: Load the default boot entry into memory:
Once a kernel is loaded, a normal reboot, for example with systemctl reboot, also uses &kexec;.
To unload the kernel and return to normal reboots, run:

systemctl kexec shuts down the system cleanly and then starts the loaded kernel. If no kernel is loaded, the command tries to find one itself. Automatic loading only works on systems that boot with UEFI and use boot entries that follow the Boot Loader Specification. Otherwise, the command fails with No kexec kernel loaded and autodetection failed. In that case, load the kernel as described in the previous step.
Once the system is back, check the kernel messages of the current boot for warnings:
Then confirm that the system is running the expected kernel:

topic.remark: ssarkar: tested on SLES 16.1 x86-64 with BIOS boot (2026-10-30): systemctl kexec without a loaded kernel fails with the autodetection message; kexec-bootloader followed by systemctl kexec reboots with kexec and uses the current /etc/default/grub options; with a kernel loaded, systemctl reboot also reboots with kexec; kexec -u unloads it. 16.0 ships the same kexec-load.service and systemd 257. Not run on UEFI, AArch64, POWER or IBM Z.

section.title: Loading a kernel manually
section.para: To start a kernel other than the default boot entry, or a kernel with different options, load it with kexec -l and name the kernel, initrd and kernel options yourself:

On &productnameshort;, kernel images are in /usr/lib/modules/KERNEL_VERSION/vmlinuz, and initrds are in /boot/initrd-KERNEL_VERSION. To reuse the kernel options of the running system, use --reuse-cmdline instead of --append.

example.title: Loading the running kernel again with its current options

section.para: Then reboot with systemctl kexec, which shuts down the system cleanly before it starts the loaded kernel. kexec -e also starts the loaded kernel, but immediately and without calling shutdown(8), so services are not stopped cleanly.
